corridor.description: Since Brexit (31 January 2020), UK nationals are third-country nationals for German immigration purposes and no longer benefit from EU free movement. The primary route for academically qualified salaried employment is the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU). The Skilled Worker visa (Fachkräfte mit akademischer Ausbildung) is the secondary route for those below the Blue Card salary threshold. UK nationals holding dual EU nationality (e.g., Irish, German) are exempt from third-country rules.

pathways.duration_basis: Standard 4 years; may be limited to employment contract duration + 3 months if shorter.

eligibility.salary_basis: No statutory minimum; salary must be customary for the position
eligibility.ba_zustimmung_label_en: Federal Employment Agency (BA) approval required for non-shortage occupations

required_documents.document_name: Post-Brexit corridor classification: UK as third country for German immigration
required_documents.description: Since Brexit, UK nationals are third-country nationals under German law and have no EU free movement rights. They must obtain a national visa (Type D) and subsequent residence title (Blaue Karte EU or Aufenthaltserlaubnis). UK nationals holding dual citizenship from an EU/EEA country are treated as EU nationals for immigration purposes.

required_documents.document_name: EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) pathway overview for UK→DE
required_documents.description: The EU Blue Card is the primary immigration route for qualified UK nationals seeking salaried employment in Germany. It requires a recognized university degree and an employment contract meeting the 2026 salary threshold (€50,700 general; €45,934.20 shortage occupations). Duration: 4 years. Fast-track (Beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren) available through employer.

required_documents.document_name: EU Blue Card eligibility criteria for UK nationals applying in Germany (2026)
required_documents.description: UK nationals qualify for the EU Blue Card if: (1) holding a university degree recognized in the Anabin database (H+) or a ZAB Statement of Comparability; (2) employment contract or binding job offer with gross annual salary ≥ €50,700 (general) or ≥ €45,934.20 for shortage occupations (IT, STEM, medicine) or recent graduates; (3) contract duration ≥ 6 months. No German language requirement.

required_documents.document_name: Beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren (fast-track) for EU Blue Card — UK→DE
required_documents.condition_expression: available when employer initiates jointly with applicant
required_documents.description: The fast-track skilled worker procedure (Beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren) allows German employers to jointly request accelerated processing with the applicant. Target processing: 21–28 days (vs 28–84 days standard). The employer must initiate the request at the local foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde). Fee: €411 (2026). This is the recommended route for time-sensitive relocations.

required_documents.document_name: Skilled Worker visa (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz) overview for UK→DE
required_documents.description: The Skilled Worker visa is the secondary route for UK nationals with a recognized degree whose salary falls below the Blue Card threshold. No statutory salary minimum. BA (Federal Employment Agency) approval required for non-shortage occupations. Duration: 4 years. Requires a job offer with customary-for-position pay.

required_documents.document_name: Dual nationality check: UK nationals with EU citizenship
required_documents.condition_expression: applicable when applicant holds dual UK + EU/EEA nationality
required_documents.description: UK nationals who also hold citizenship of an EU or EEA member state (e.g., Irish passport, German citizenship acquired through naturalisation or ancestry) are treated as EU/EEA nationals for German immigration. They may enter and work under EU free movement rules without a Blue Card or skilled worker permit. This should be checked before applying for a third-country visa.

required_documents.document_name: Path classifier: default to EU Blue Card for qualified UK nationals at or above salary threshold
required_documents.description: Default pathway for UK nationals with a recognized degree and gross annual salary ≥ €50,700: route to EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU). This is the preferred route as it provides a 4-year residence title, faster settlement eligibility (21 months with B1 German; 33 months without), and portability within the EU.

required_documents.document_name: Path classifier: Blue Card shortage occupation — reduced salary threshold for UK nationals
required_documents.description: For shortage occupations (IT specialists, physicians, STEM engineers, mathematicians, scientists), the Blue Card salary threshold is reduced to €45,934.20. BA approval is still required. The employer should confirm the occupation is on the shortage list (Positivliste) before applying.

required_documents.document_name: Path classifier: fallback to Skilled Worker visa for UK nationals below Blue Card threshold
required_documents.description: UK nationals with a recognized degree but gross annual salary below €45,934.20 are routed to the Skilled Worker visa (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz). Salary must be customary for the position. BA (Federal Employment Agency) approval is required for non-shortage occupations. Processing is similar to Blue Card but without the premium EU portability benefit.

required_documents.document_name: Visa application process at German Consulate General London for UK nationals
required_documents.description: UK-resident applicants must apply for the national visa (Type D) at the German Consulate General in London. Appointments can be booked online via the Consulate website. The visa (Type D, 'Blaue Karte EU Zweck') is typically issued for 90 days; the multi-year Blue Card residence title is then issued by the local Ausländerbehörde after arrival and Anmeldung.

required_documents.document_name: Official processing times for UK→DE Blue Card — standard and fast-track
required_documents.description: Standard Blue Card processing at the German Consulate in London: 4–12 weeks (28–84 days). Fast-track (Beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren, employer-initiated): 3–4 weeks (21–28 days). The fast-track route requires the employer to apply first at the Ausländerbehörde; the consulate appointment is then granted within the accelerated timeline. Source: BAMF 2026 data.

required_documents.document_name: Valid UK passport (biometric, with at least 6 months validity beyond visa expiry)
UK university degree certificate + transcripts (with apostille and sworn German or English translation)
required_documents.book_early_reason: UK FCDO apostille: 2–5 business days legalisation; sworn German translation adds 1–2 weeks. Start at least 3 weeks before visa appointment.

required_documents.document_name: Signed employment contract or binding job offer — gross annual salary ≥ €50,700 (general) or ≥ €45,934.20 (shortage / recent graduate)
National visa application form (Type D — Blue Card purpose, signed)
Birth certificate (UK apostille + sworn German translation); marriage certificate if accompanied by spouse

post_arrival_steps.name: Anmeldung — register address with local Bürgeramt
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Bundesmeldegesetz §17 — within 2 weeks of moving in.
post_arrival_steps.where: Local city registration office (Bürgeramt / KVR / Meldeamt)

post_arrival_steps.name: Open German bank account (required for salary payments)
Collect electronic residence title (Blaue Karte EU eAT) at Ausländerbehörde
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Entry visa (Type D, 90 days) requires conversion to multi-year residence title in person at the Ausländerbehörde.
post_arrival_steps.fee_label: eAT card fee (typical; varies by Ausländerbehörde)
post_arrival_steps.where: Local Ausländerbehörde — book appointment after Anmeldung

path_classifier_rules.rationale: Default Blue Card pathway for qualified UK professionals meeting the 2026 general salary threshold.
Reduced salary threshold for shortage occupations (IT, STEM, medicine).
Below the Blue Card threshold — route to Skilled Worker visa (no statutory salary minimum, BA approval required).

known_gaps: Dual nationality (UK + EU) check must be surfaced before applying for a third-country visa — currently manual.
Salary thresholds reviewed annually; re-verify at next_review_due.
Family reunification for UK nationals is out of scope for this corridor file.
Settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) at 21/33 months and German B1 requirement is referenced but not fully encoded as a downstream pathway.
